name: B. and B. (Old Jackass) deposit
tonnage: small copper-silver-gold property with little production
quote: The owners report that samples of sorted ore averaged 5-6 percent copper, 14-15 ounces of silver, and $2.80 in gold per ton.

name: Allured mine (Oxide workings, 1947 carload)
tonnage: one carload; several hundred tons silver-gold-copper ore 1925-40
quote: In 1947 one carload of ore mined from the 85-foot level averaged 8 percent copper and $6 or more in gold and silver.

name: Copper World mine
anchor_hint: Clark Mountain, NW of Mountain Pass
tonnage: yield greater than 1,000,000 pounds of copper
quote: The Copper World workings lie along a zone in which copper minerals, principally malachite and azurite, exist in veinlets and irregular bodies. The ore, as mined is said to have averaged 2 percent copper.

name: Gold Hill Copper mine (1939 shipment)
quote: From this stope came the ore shipment reported in 1939. This was shipped to Hayden, Arizona, and assayed 5.45 percent copper, 0.425 ounce of gold and 54 cents in silver per ton.

name: Horn mine
anchor_hint: Turtle Mountains, west of Vidal Junction
quote: Four shipments totaling about 200 tons have been made. The grade of ore shipped has ranged from 4.84 to 6.71 percent copper, with small amounts of gold.

name: Little Mike mine
tonnage: approximately 40 tons of copper-silver ore, wholly in 1949
quote: The ore, according to Roy V. Waughtel, the former lessee, averaged about 5i percent copper and 3-| ounces of silver per ton.

name: New American Eagle (American Eagle) mine
anchor_hint: Whipple Mountains, NE of Vidal Junction
quote: The total production has been about 700 tons which averaged about 8 percent copper.

name: New Trail mine (Anchor workings, 1947-50 output)
anchor_hint: SE of Mountain Pass, east of Baker
tonnage: ore valued at about $12,000 mined in the period
quote: The mine was operated from 1947 to 1950 by W. H. Hile, and in 1950-51 by Alloy Mining Company. Copper-gold-silver ore, valued at about $12,000 was mined in that period. The ore averaged about 7 ounces in silver, 5.73 ounces in gold and 6.2 percent copper.

name: Ord Mountain mine (Brilliant claim, 1942 lot)
quote: ore averaging between two and three percent copper and $7.75 gold.

name: Ord Mountain mine (Rio Vista claim, 1942 stopes)
quote: These ore bodies were stoped in 1942, yielding over 1,000 tons of ore averaging nearly two percent copper and $5.51 in gold.

name: Standard No. 2 mine
tonnage: over five thousand dollars worth of copper-gold-silver ore
quote: The shaft is reported 30 to be 275 feet deep, and to have yielded over five thousand dollars worth of copper-gold-silver ore from its 100- and 150-foot levels. One shipment assayed 13 percent copper, 8 dollars in gold, and 16 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Von Trigger (California Gold and Copper, Dutch Oven) mine
quote: was obtained in the period 1926-1929, when the property was worked by the California Gold and Copper Company ; shipments totaled 77 cars or 3729 tons of ore averaging 5.03 percent copper.

name: Desert Antimony mine
anchor_hint: east base of Clark Mountain, NE of Mountain Pass
tonnage: small tonnages 1927-28 and 1939; sorted to 40 percent
quote: The ore as mined is reported to have carried from 15 to 20 percent antimony and to have been sorted to a grade of 40 percent.

name: Bagdad Chase mine (1904-10 Barstow mill run)
quote: From 1904 to 1910 the mine was operated by the Bagdad-Chase Mining Company, which treated 150,000 tons of ore at its mill in Barstow, using the cyanide process and recovering gold only. The total value of gold recovered was $4,500,000.

name: Bagdad Chase mine (Pacific Mines smelter shipments)
quote: During the following 6 years, when the mine was operated by the Pacific Mines Corporation, 120,000 tons of copper-gold ore was shipped to a smelter at Clarkdale, Arizona. This output had an average grade of 1.82 percent copper, 0.35 ounces of gold and 1.5 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Black Hawk mine (Randsburg)
quote: The Black Hawk mine, generally and erroneously described as being in Kern County, operated almost continuously from 1896 to 1942. It has yielded about $700,000 in free milling gold obtained from ore assaying between $12 and $60 per ton.

name: Brannigan mine (high-grade carloads)
anchor_hint: Old Dad Mountain, SE of Baker
tonnage: several thousand tons of gold ore
quote: ore shipments were confined to the period 1928-1935 when the mine was most actively worked. It has yielded several thousand tons of gold ore, carloads of which are said to have averaged as much as $110 per ton.

name: Brooklyn mine (Dale district)
anchor_hint: Dale district, east of Twentynine Palms
quote: Free gold occurs associated with iron oxides and oxidized copper minerals. Some of the ore developed had a value of $16 per ton in gold and contained 1 to 3 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Carlyle mine (winze ore shoot)
anchor_hint: Pinto Mountains, SE of Twentynine Palms
tonnage: ore shoot 60 feet long, 6 feet wide
quote: These winze workings developed an ore shoot 60 feet long and 6 feet wide, reported to average $12 per ton in gold ; the gold values were principally on the hanging wall, and high grade silver ore was reported on the footwall.

name: Carlyle mine (mill heads)
anchor_hint: Pinto Mountains, SE of Twentynine Palms
quote: Mill heads were reported to carry $10 to $20 per ton in gold and $3 to $6 per ton in silver.

name: Doble (Gold Mountain, Lucky Baldwin) mine
quote: When operated in the late 1930 's, the ore is believed to have averaged $6 per ton.

name: Keystone mine (Stoddard Mountain)
quote: The gold occurs as fine flour gold, bearing some silver. Assays as high as $800 are reported, but most of the ore is said to have run about $50 per ton.

name: Olympus (Paradise) mine
anchor_hint: Paradise Mountains, south of Paradise Spring
quote: The gold as mined is reported to have been free-milling and to have averaged about $6 per ton.

name: Rio Hondo mine
quote: The principal workings explore a vein that is several hundred feet long and mostly 2 to 5 feet wide. Much of the vein is said to assay $7 to $15 per ton in gold which is partly free and partly in auriferous pyrite.

name: Rose mine (high-grade shipments)
district: Rose mine area, San Bernardino Mountains (San Bernardino)
quote: The gold is said to occur in a quartz-calcite gangue associated with much hematite ; some shipments are reported to have been valued at $200 to $500 per ton.

name: Santa Fe mines (Arlington-Santa Fe lode reserves)
district: Blackhawk Canyon, San Bernardino Mountains (San Bernardino)
anchor_hint: 5 airline miles north of Baldwin Lake
tonnage: known reserves measurable in millions of tons
quote: Although a few relatively small bodies were found to average more than $30 per ton, the known reserves, measurable in millions of tons, are said to be valued in the range of $1.20 to $11 per ton.

name: Supply mine group (Nightingale ore shoot)
anchor_hint: Dale district, 20 miles SE of Twentynine Palms
quote: These workings developed an ore shoot 250 feet long and 9 feet in average width. The ore mined was reported to have averaged $12 per ton in gold.

name: Telegraph mine (remaining ore)
quote: The owner reports that considerable tonnages of ore ranging in grade from $8 to $14 per ton remain in the mine.

name: Vanderbilt mine (Gold Bar 16-car shipment)
anchor_hint: New York Mountains, ESE of Ivanpah
tonnage: 16-car shipment; output several hundred thousand dollars
quote: A typical 16-car shipment from the Gold Bar workings is said to have averaged 0.72 ounce gold, 3.50 ounces silver, 0.50 percent copper, and 0.80 percent lead

name: Virginia Dale mine
anchor_hint: Dale district, 18 miles SE of Twentynine Palms
quote: Free gold in the quartz veins is associated with hematite, magnetite and manganese oxides. Gold values range from $9 to $20 per ton, averaging $12 per ton.

name: Blue Bell (Hard Luck) mine
tonnage: total output about 80 tons of lead-silver-copper ore
quote: The ore, composed principally of chrysocolla, malachite, cerussite, galena, and chalcopyrite in a carbonate gangue, is reported by the lessee to have averaged about 11 percent lead, 4-J percent copper, and 4 ounces of silver per ton.

name: C. and K. (Bell Gilroy) mine
quote: The ore as mined is reported to have contained 6 to 12 percent lead and about 20 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Carbonate King Zinc mine (1940-44 production)
anchor_hint: Kokoweef Peak, SE of Mountain Pass
quote: From 1940 to 1944, the deposits yielded about 4,000 tons of ore averaging 35.5 percent zinc, 1.0 percent lead, and 10 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Carbonate King Zinc mine (1949 shipment)
anchor_hint: Kokoweef Peak, SE of Mountain Pass
quote: About 500 tons of ore, assaying 40 percent zinc, was shipped in 1949 to International Smelting and Refining at Tooele, Utah.

name: Cucamonga Zinc (Blew Jordam) deposit (channel samples)
district: Lytle Creek, San Gabriel Mountains (San Bernardino)
anchor_hint: head of East Fork of Lytle Creek, north of Fontana
quote: The owner reports that channel samples, taken through widths of 5 to 6 feet, have assayed 3.2 to 13.1 percent zinc, from a trace to 3.6 percent lead, and from 0.3 to 6.65 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Death Valley mine (main stope shipments)
district: Mid Hills, New York Mountains (San Bernardino)
tonnage: total yield of lead-silver-gold ore valued about $131,000
quote: An ore shoot, 400 feet long, was stoped from the 200-foot level to the surface. The ore shipped from this stope is reported by the owner to have averaged 75 ounces of silver, and 0.18 ounces of gold per ton, and 2.5 percent lead.

name: Death Valley mine (second vein milling ore)
district: Mid Hills, New York Mountains (San Bernardino)
quote: The other vein, encountered by a 138-foot cross-cut from the 400-foot level, yielded 500 tons of milling ore which the owner reports averaged 17 ounces of silver, 0.10 ounce of gold, 2.5 percent lead, and 1.5 percent zinc.

name: Mitchell mine (dump ore)
anchor_hint: near Mitchell's Caverns, NW of Essex
tonnage: 250 tons of ore on the dump
quote: They have shipped no ore but report that 250 tons of ore on the dump will assay 15 percent lead and 5 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Mohawk mine (Clark Mountain, 1951 shipments)
anchor_hint: Mohawk Hill, west of Clark Mountain Station
quote: The operators report that recent shipments to Selby, California, have averaged 8 to 10 percent lead, 3 percent zinc, and 7 to 8 ounces of silver. From May 1951 to December 1951, about 640 tons was shipped.

name: Nigger Mountain (Fremont, Mohawk Zinc) mine
district: Cushenbury Canyon, San Bernardino Mountains (San Bernardino)
quote: The ore shipped to the U. S. Smelting, Refining, and Mining Company, Midvale, Utah, assayed 22 percent lead, 7 percent zinc, and 20 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Silver Rule (Chambers) mine
quote: The principal ore minerals are galena and secondary minerals of lead and zinc. Much of the ore mined in the earlier period assayed 20 to 40 percent lead, 7 to 10 percent zinc, and 10 to 20 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Yucca Metals mine (1917 shipment)
quote: The Yucca Metals mine is a lead-silver deposit just east of the Mohawk mine described above. The lead ores occur in fractures in limestone. Two cars of ore shipped in 1917, carried 19 to 24 percent lead and 5 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Calico district
tonnage: district total estimated 13 to 20 million dollars
quote: The average value of the Calico ores was 10 to 20 ounces of silver per ton, but high-grade pockets of cerargyrite or native silver yielded ore valued at as much as $2000 per ton.

name: Silver King and Oriental group (Calico)
quote: During the four years 1883 to 1886 the mine yielded 37,000 tons of ore with a gross value of $1,355,000 or $36.61 per ton in silver.

name: Garfield mine (Calico, September 1883 bonanza lot)
quote: In September, 96 tons yielded $8,736 and nine tons yielded $7,200, or about 800 ounces per ton.

name: Garfield mine (Calico, 1883-84 output)
quote: The output from November 1883 through 1884 included 2400 tons of ore that yielded $290,400, as well as other ore not recorded.

name: Langtry mine (Calico)
quote: The ore is reported to have averaged from 6 to 22 ounces of silver per ton.

name: Waterloo mine (Calico)
tonnage: supplied two stamp mills at Daggett
quote: The ore is reported to have averaged from 11 to 20 ounces of silver per ton, but some shipments assayed as high as 1000 ounces.

name: Voca mine (Calico)
anchor_hint: east of the Waterloo, west of Calico
tonnage: 10 to 15 tons daily; total output small
quote: Most of the mining was done before 1888. During much of its active period the mine daily yielded 10 to 15 tons of ore averaging 40 ounces of silver per ton, but the total output was small.

name: Burcham (Total Wreck) mine (Mulcahy vein)
anchor_hint: one mile west of Calico townsite
tonnage: substantial tonnage of $15 ore from 26-inch footwall zone
quote: The Mulcahy ranges from 4 to 30 feet wide. Its ore probably averaged about $6.50 per ton in gold and silver. A substantial tonnage of ore with an average value of about $15 per ton was obtained from a zone, 26 inches wide, along the footwall.

name: Randsburg district (Red Mountain silver veins, richest ore bodies)
quote: The largest of the rich ore bodies were found to contain 25,000 to 50,000 tons of ore with average values of $70 to $100 per ton. With depth the mineralization appears to decrease in silver and increase in gold.

name: Kelly (California Rand) mine (1919 discovery samples)
quote: Williams believed he recognized horn silver in the outcrop and samples were brought to Kelly who confirmed the identification through a Bakersfield assayer. The samples were found to contain $300 of silver and 3 ounces of gold per ton.

name: Kelly (California Rand) mine (Grady lease output)
quote: In the 14-month period, ending February 1, 1922, the Grady lease yielded 18,245 tons of ore valued at $1,613,074.

name: Akron-Silver Reef deposit
anchor_hint: 12 airline miles southeast of Lucerne Valley
quote: The operators state that the ore minerals are confined to the matrix, and that the average value of the material sampled to date is between $3 and $3.25 per ton.

name: Waterman mine
quote: It consists of a barite-jasper gangue containing native silver and silver sulfides. Silver chlorides exist near the surface. The ore averaged about 41^ ounces of silver per ton, according to the owner.

name: Atolia mines (Atolia Mining Company ore, 1909-43)
quote: Previous to the initiation of the large-scale, open-cut mining methods in 1943, the ore mined and milled by the Atolia Mining Company since 1909 probably averaged slightly more than 4 percent W03. Yearly averages ran as low as one percent and as high as 15 percent.

name: Hidden Value mine
anchor_hint: north end of Old Woman Mountains, near Danby
quote: From early 1943 through 1945 a total of 333 units of W03 was produced from ore which, according to the owner, averaged 2.75 percent W03.

name: Howe Tungsten (Section 9) mine
anchor_hint: north end of Old Woman Mountains, SE of Danby
quote: This property was first mined during 1944 when, according to the owner, it yielded 218 tens of ore averaging 4.35 percent W03.

name: Starbright Tungsten mine
anchor_hint: 21 miles north of Barstow, near Lane Mountain
quote: By mid-1951 the mine had yielded over 10,000 tons of ore averaging 1-J to 2 percent W03, the largest output of any San Bernardino County tungsten mine outside of the Atolia district.

name: White Dollar mine
quote: Some of the ore is reported by the lessees to have assayed 1.4 percent W03, but the average grade was probably less than 1 percent W03.
